rv.q: Minor niggles aside, Frayn's comic classic seems to be bulletproof.
It calls for acting larger-than-life and inch-perfect. It gets it.
Frayn's ingenious farce-within-a-farce sees a clunky touring production of a faded bedroom farce, Nothing On, fall apart around the performers' ears.
The entire thing breezes away the January blues with glorious brilliance. It is an utter treasure.
Noises Off is superbly clever and wildly funny... it remains a masterclass in farce.
It has an entertaining structure and premise, it just feels dated.

cn.t: Frayn's farce-within-a-farce remains a clever, wildly funny masterclass in comedy, with critics praising the cast's inch-perfect performances. Some find it slightly dated compared to modern successors, but most agree it's a brilliantly executed treasure.
